metadata.case_name: LAI PING WAH v. CHINA INSURANCE CO. LTD. AND ANOTEHR

source: Head injury with laceration.
Forehead laceration
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

injuries.description: Left leg laceration (deep to muscle, debrided and sutured)
source: Left leg laceration - (this was also recorded in a diagram as 7 cm deep to muscle).
left leg laceration (now noted as 8 cm deep to muscle).
Debridément and Suturing on 11/9 [This must refer to the left leg laceration.]
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of lower leg

injuries.description: Open injury over right shoulder (left to heal of its own accord)
source: An open injury over her right shoulder was left to heal of its own accord;
injuries.icd_description: Open wound of shoulder or upper arm, unspecified

injuries.description: Fracture of the left inferior pubic ramus
source: The discharge/transfer summary dated 26th October, some six weeks or so after the accident, refers to a fracture of the left inferior pubic ramus and also of the right little toe, as well as the left leg laceration.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of pubis without disruption of pelvic ring

injuries.description: Fracture of the right little toe
source: The discharge/transfer summary dated 26th October, some six weeks or so after the accident, refers to a fracture of the left inferior pubic ramus and also of the right little toe, as well as the left leg laceration.

injuries.description: Optic neuritis leading to blindness (left then right eye; eventual total blindness)
source: In February 1995 there was some complaint of frontal scalp pain; by July 1995 she was blind in her left eye, retrobulbar neuritis having been diagnosed in April, and there was deterioration in vision in her right eye.
"Gradual onset of loss of vision of left eye over five days....."
Total blindness of left eye.
MR1 scan of orbit on 25th May 1996 showed abnormal enhancement of left optic nerve.

injuries.body_part: central nervous system / spinal cord and optic nerves
source: Either the injuries themselves or the contamination, or the necessary tetanus toxoid injections, collectively or individually, led to the development of Devic's Syndrome - and I accept Dr. Huang's view that this was probably a case of Devic's, independent of Multiple Sclerosis.

The diagnosis was recorded as Optical neuritis leading to idiopathy or secondary demyelinating disease (multiplesclerosis). An entry for the 18th July 1995 records as the diagnosis "bilateral Optic Neuritis."
Her diagnosis has been variously recorded as multiple sclerosis, Devic's Syndrome and other forms of demyelinating disease but the overall tendency has been to apply the label of multiple sclerosis.

injuries.description: Transverse myelitis / spinal cord lesion (changes at T4-T10 on MRI)
source: MR1 scan of the spine on 19th October 1995 showed changes at T4-T10.
14th May, 1996 noting bilateral lower limb twitching and weakness with a diagnosis of multiple sclerosis - transverse myelitis (inflammatory disease of the spinal cord).
injuries.icd_description: Other incomplete cord syndrome of thoracic spinal cord

source: She became totally blind in or about March 1996 and there was progressive weakness in her legs requiring her to use a frame to walk.
Paraplegia had set in from about May 1996 onwards and further deterioration led to tetraplegia.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of cervical spinal cord, unspecified

manifestations.description: Back pain with tenderness T6 to T8 region.
Reduced sensation / numbness over right forehead / supraorbital nerve distribution.
Gradual onset of loss of vision of left eye over five days; Total blindness of left eye.
Deterioration in vision of right eye leading to total blindness.
Progressive weakness in her legs requiring her to use a frame to walk.
Paraesthesiae and numbness over the right upper face (paraesthesia of right V1 and V2).
Reduced power in her lower limbs and she was chair bound.
Dizziness (transient episodes after X-ray and on other dates).

treatments_received.treatment: Suturing of facial wound (10/9) under local anaesthetic
source: The Nursing Kardex (Sheet A) notes:
Suturing of facial wound 10/9.
Sheet B of the Nursing Kardex which records the progress and intervention and evaluation, confirms that the facial laceration was sutured on the ward under local anaesthetic on 10th September.

treatments_received.treatment: Debridement and suturing of left leg wound (11/9)
source: Debridément and Suturing on 11/9 [This must refer to the left leg laceration.]
The operation record of 11th September deals with the wound to the left calf region.

treatments_received.treatment: Exploration of wounds under local anaesthetic (14/9)
source: Also on the 14th September is recorded exploration of wounds under local anaesthetic without more detail.

treatments_received.treatment: Removal of pieces of broken glass from right hand and left leg (28/9) and possibly elbow (29/9)
source: Thereafter little of note is recorded save possibly the removal of pieces of broken glass from right hand and left leg on the 28th September and a piece of glass from the elbow, possibly, on the following day.
treatments_received.vmis_procedure: Incision and / or removal of foreign body from skin and subcutaneous tissue

treatments_received.treatment: Further debridement and drainage by reason of infection (7th October)
source: At the time she was writing her health had already taken a serious downturn though she makes no mention of those developments.
It required further debridément and drainage by reason of infection on the 7th October, almost one month later.
treatments_received.vmis_procedure: Incision and / or drainage of skin abscess

source: On the 12th September a neck collar was applied and there was a complaint of dizziness after the X-ray was taken, which persisted through the 13th & 14th September in a mild form.

treatments_received.treatment: Tetanus toxoid injections (initial on day of accident; booster 22nd October 1994; further booster 20th April 1995)
source: the number of tetanus toxoid injections she received and their timing. The first was on the day of the accident. The second, a booster was on the 22nd October and the third, a further booster was on the 20th April 1995.
She suffered severe visual loss leading to blindness in the left eye after the first attack of optic neuritis; then blindness in the right eye despite steroid therapy.

treatments_received.treatment: Radiological and diagnostic investigations (X-rays, CT scan, MRI scans of orbit, brain and spine, myelogram, CSF examinations, brainstem auditory evoked potentials)
source: X-rays of skill and cervical spine were normal on 12th September 1994. CT scan of skull orbit on 29th April 1995 showed no abnormality. MR1 scan of orbit on 25th May 1996 showed abnormal enhancement of left optic nerve.
MR1 scans of brain dated 25th May 1995 and 26th December 1995, 12th September 1996 and 7th November 1997 showed absence of brain parenchymal lesion.
Myelogram of the whole spine on 16th October 1995 showed no abnormality
MR1 scan of the spine on 19th October 1995 showed changes at T4-T10.
CSF examinations on 8th July and 16th October 1995 demonstrated an absence of oligoclonal bands. Brainstem auditory evoked potential on 18th July and 17th October 1995 showed no abnormality.

losses.description: Permanent cosmetic disfigurement from facial lacerations.
Loss of sight (left eye in April 1995 with progressive loss of right eye leading to total blindness).
Decline from hemi-paresis to paraplegia and being wheelchair bound, ultimately quadriplegia.
Persistent decline and dependency on others with little realistic hope of reversal.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Deceased required substantial services from her husband; many domestic tasks had to be performed by him.
